subject: soda vending machine
title: What If You Rocked a Vending Machine for a Free Soda?

scenes.text: What if you rocked a vending machine for a free soda? The machine often wins.
A loaded soda machine weighs hundreds of pounds, and almost all of it is high up.
Rock it far enough and all that weight swings past the tipping point, straight at you.
US safety regulators counted at least 37 deaths and 113 injuries from falling machines since 1978.
So makers added anti-tip devices and warning stickers: it will not dispense free product.
A 1988 medical report found fifteen young men hurt this way. Three of them died. For one can of soda.

description:
What if you rocked a vending machine? The US Consumer Product Safety Commission counted at least 37 deaths and 113 injuries from tipped machines since 1978.
That led to anti-tip devices and the famous warning label: never rock or tilt, machine can fall over, will not dispense free product.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Have you ever had a vending machine eat your money? What everyday object should we put through a what-if next?
